SEBoK Verification and Validation Strategy, Distilled

Fifth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 1 of 5 (SE-161). Second SE-internal distillation of V&V Strategy (the prior pass at SE-086 read it as Cluster B independence-by-design fourth composition rule). Target page is 404; the article is dispersed across System Verification and System Validation. Section 3.1 of System Validation supplies the canonical phrase: "the efficiency of system realization is gained by optimizing the three strategies together to form what is often called the verification and validation strategy." Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument pattern at moderate density. The fifth-sweep revisit folds the SE-086 reading against §VII.7's matured taxonomy. Cluster B independence-by-design (fourth composition rule, formalized) holds; the V&V-strategy is the canonical worked example. Cluster A surfaces a three-axis universal-sibling lattice at the strategy rung: verification-strategy / validation-strategy / integration-strategy are universal-sibling siblings at the realization-engagement rung; this is the sub-form's first three-axis instance among V&V-strategy readings. Cluster F backward-pulverization paired-V&V structural discriminator (formalized at SE-160) applies. The "joint optimization" framing is structurally a Cluster D co-production at the strategy rung between three substrate-keepers. Six clusters compose.

II. Source Read

The target page does not exist. The V&V strategy is carried by Section 3.1 of System Validation, which states verbatim: "the efficiency of system realization is gained by optimizing the three strategies together to form what is often called the verification and validation strategy." This optimization defines and performs the minimum number of V&V actions while detecting maximum errors and achieving confidence in the system. Validation is "a transverse activity to every life cycle stage" running parallel to system definition and realization. Coordination occurs with project managers (schedule, resources), designers (issue/trouble reports), and configuration managers (baselines, versions). Cross-references include System Verification, System Realization, System Transition, System Operation. The V&V strategy itself is therefore composite: a planning artifact that joins three strategies (verification, validation, integration) into a single optimization.

III. Structural Read

Editorial-state observation. Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument pattern at moderate density. The V&V strategy lives distributed across System Verification (SE-160 / SE-025), System Validation (SE-029), and System Realization (SE-041). No standalone page; the formalization rung is internal-migration mode (per SE-039 §VII.7's four-mode taxonomy: bidirectional-fold, internal-migration, external-migration, dual-discipline-distribution). This is an internal-migration instance: the V&V-strategy formalization migrated into the surrounding V&V pages rather than out to a standards-body ecosystem.

Cluster A (universal-sibling lattice, Doc 572 Appendix D), three-axis strategy-rung lattice. Section 3.1's "three strategies" framing surfaces a Cluster A lattice at the strategy rung: verification-strategy, validation-strategy, integration-strategy. Each strategy binds every system-realization engagement aspect-wise; the discriminator is question-answered, not rung-of-application (verification: have we built it right; validation: have we built the right thing; integration: do the parts compose). Three-axis universal-sibling lattice at the strategy rung; first instance at the V&V-strategy rung specifically. Adjacent to SE-160's three-nested lattices.

Cluster B (multi-keeper composition, Doc 604), independence-by-design fourth composition rule, formalized worked example. SE-086 read V&V Strategy as the canonical Cluster B independence-by-design instance (the fourth composition rule, asserting non-composition rather than mode-of-composition). The fifth-sweep revisit confirms: validator-keeper, verifier-keeper, and integrator-keeper compose at the strategy rung specifically by maintaining structural independence at the substrate-evidence rung. The "minimum number of V&V actions while detecting maximum errors" framing is the optimization that the independence rule operationalizes. Cluster B density gains; SE-086 stays the anchor for the fourth rule.

Cluster F (pulverization, Doc 445), paired-V&V anchor, structural discriminator applies. The V&V-strategy is the planning instrument that produces the paired pulverization $T = \langle T_I, T_E \rangle$. SE-160's binary-comparison-vs-value-judgment discriminator is the strategy's primary partition: the strategy must allocate to verification anything binary-comparable and to validation anything that requires value-judgment. The "minimum number of actions" optimization runs over the union of these two pulverization disciplines. SE-161 reaffirms SE-160's discriminator as load-bearing.

Cluster D (co-production at sub-rungs, Doc 573), strategy-rung joint optimization. The "optimizing the three strategies together" framing is structurally co-production at the strategy rung between three substrate-keepers: verification-substrate (objective-evidence-keeper), validation-substrate (operational-intent-keeper), integration-substrate (composition-coherence-keeper). The strategy artifact is jointly authored by all three; no single keeper alone produces it. Cluster D gains a strategy-rung instance at the multi-keeper-co-production sub-form.

Cluster K (virtue constraints, Doc 314), V3-as-procedure-binding at the optimization rung. The "minimum actions while maximum errors detected" framing is V3 in procedural form: the procedure binds the strategy against the rankism risk that the planner ranks one strategy above the others (e.g., privileging verification because it is binary, deferring validation because it is judgment-laden). The strategy procedure forces all three to compose. Cluster K density grows; SE-161 supplies a strategy-planning sub-mode of V3-as-procedure-binding.

Cluster H (hypostatic boundary, Doc 372). The strategy describes activity coordination, not metaphysical claims. Standard hypostatic discipline.

V. Residuals

No structural residuals against the apparatus. The dispersed-instrument pattern accommodates the article-absence; the carrier sections supply enough quotable structural framing to read all six clusters cleanly.

Internal-migration mode confirmed. The V&V-strategy is internal-migration (formalization lives in surrounding SEBoK pages) rather than external-migration (Open SE, Design-to-Cost). This complements the §VII.7 four-mode taxonomy at a lower migration-distance.

Cluster D strategy-rung co-production worked example. The "optimizing together" framing is the cleanest strategy-rung co-production reading observed; SE-161 is a worked-example candidate for Doc 573's strategy-rung sub-form.
